title: Priya's wedding
subtitle: Un matrimonio canadese
intro: A Hindu ceremony on Saturday morning, a Canadian reception on Saturday night: mehndi, a registry, RSVP, a cash bar, speeches that are funny on purpose, a dance floor where Doug does the Macarena. Chiara gives a one-minute toast and makes the room laugh in English. Crossover with [[IT Unit 23]]. This unit builds the full [[gerund vs infinitive]] system, [[both / neither / either / all / none]], the first [[participle phrases]] ([[walking in, I saw]]), the [[idioms]] every B1 learner needs, and [[make vs do]].
objectives: Scegliere -ing o to-infinito dopo i verbi: [[I enjoy baking]], [[I decided to leave]], [[I remember meeting her]] vs [[remember to call]]
Usare both / neither / either / all / none per quantità con due o più: [[both are coming]], [[neither of us can dance]]
Usare frasi participiali di apertura: [[Walking into the hall, I saw…]]
Capire e usare idiomi inglesi: [[tie the knot]], [[over the moon]], [[break the ice]], [[cold feet]]
Distinguere make e do: [[make a decision / do the dishes]]
canDo: B1 · Spoken interaction: can take part in a social event with speeches, jokes and small-talk.
B1 · Spoken production: can give a short toast or speech in English.
B1 · Listening: can follow humour and idioms at natural speed.
B1 · Writing: can write a short formal thank-you note or an RSVP.
B1 · Lexis: knows the vocabulary of weddings in a Canadian multicultural context.

sections.title: Mehndi, the ceremony, the reception
sections.intro: Three scenes: Thursday mehndi night at Priya's parents' home; Saturday morning Hindu ceremony at a mandap; Saturday night reception at Toronto Botanical Garden with Chiara's one-minute toast. Listen for gerund vs infinitive, both/neither/either, participle phrases, and the idioms of a wedding.

blocks.title: Thursday · the mehndi night
blocks.setting: Thursday 20 August, 7 p.m., Priya's parents' home in Scarborough. The front room filled with women — Priya's cousins, aunts, close friends, Sofia and Chiara included. A henna artist at the centre; music and tea; two long tables with sweets and savoury snacks.

lines.t: Chiara, Sofia, thank you for coming. The mehndi tonight is for the women; the men do their own thing tomorrow. Having thought about it for months, we decided to invite everybody who's close — both my friends from the bakery and my family cousins from India. Neither side has met the other, which should be interesting.
lines.n: Chiara, Sofia, grazie di essere venute. Il mehndi stasera è per le donne; gli uomini fanno il loro domani. Avendoci pensato per mesi, abbiamo deciso di invitare tutti quelli che ci sono vicini — sia le mie amiche della pasticceria che le mie cugine dall'India. Nessuna delle due parti ha conosciuto l'altra, cosa che sarà interessante.
lines.note: Having thought about it for months: participle phrase (= because we have thought). We decided to invite: decide + to + inf. Both my friends and my family: both X and Y. Neither side has met the other: neither of + sing. verb.

lines.t: What should I do with my hands? — Priya's cousin Meera will do the mehndi. You can choose a simple pattern — I'd suggest avoiding anything that goes above your wrist. If you want to try the sweets, both the gulab jamun and the barfi are from Lahore Tikka House — do try them.
lines.n: Cosa faccio con le mani? — La cugina di Priya, Meera, farà il mehndi. Puoi scegliere un disegno semplice — ti suggerirei di evitare qualcosa che vada oltre il polso. Se vuoi provare i dolci, sia il gulab jamun che il barfi sono di Lahore Tikka House — provali.
lines.note: I'd suggest avoiding: suggest + -ing (not + to). Do try them: do + bare verb for emphasis in an invitation.

lines.t: I used to be afraid of henna — I made the mistake of trying it in Marrakech ten years ago and had an orange hand for three weeks. Now I know to go to a trained artist. — You should talk to Meera. She's done this for a thousand hands.
lines.n: Avevo paura dell'henné — ho commesso l'errore di provarlo a Marrakech dieci anni fa e ho avuto una mano arancione per tre settimane. Adesso so di andare da un'artista qualificata. — Dovresti parlare con Meera. L'ha fatto a mille mani.
lines.note: I used to be afraid: used to + base (past habit). I made the mistake of trying: make the mistake of + -ing. I know to go: know + to + inf. (= know enough to).

lines.t: Marcus and Doug are both nervous about tomorrow. Neither of them has been to a Hindu wedding before. I told them to wear what they'd wear to a cathedral wedding, which is a suit, and to be ready for a long ceremony. Doug asked if there would be a cash bar. — At a mehndi, no.
lines.n: Marcus e Doug sono entrambi nervosi per domani. Nessuno dei due è mai stato a un matrimonio induista. Ho detto loro di indossare quello che indosserebbero a un matrimonio in cattedrale, che è un vestito, e di essere pronti per una cerimonia lunga. Doug ha chiesto se ci fosse un cash bar. — A un mehndi, no.
lines.note: Both nervous: adjective with both. Neither of them has been: neither of + sing. verb. If there would be a cash bar: reported if-question.

lines.t: The mehndi is good for breaking the ice between the two families. By midnight everyone will know everyone. Having been through this at my sister's wedding in Bangalore, I can tell you: Priya's cousins can out-dance anyone. Including Doug.
lines.n: Il mehndi è utile per rompere il ghiaccio fra le due famiglie. Entro mezzanotte tutti conosceranno tutti. Avendo passato questo al matrimonio di mia sorella a Bangalore, posso dirti: i cugini di Priya ballano meglio di chiunque. Doug compreso.
lines.note: Breaking the ice: idiom. Having been through: participle phrase past. Can out-dance: emphatic do with out- prefix.

notes.phrase: we decided to invite · suggest avoiding · the mistake of trying · know to go · breaking the ice · having thought · having been through
notes.note: Decide + to-inf; suggest + -ing; make the mistake of + -ing; know + to-inf (modal-ish); break the ice (idiom); participle phrases.

notes.phrase: both my friends and my family · neither side has met · neither of them has been · both nervous · gulab jamun · barfi · Lahore Tikka House
notes.note: Both / neither patterns, with multicultural food vocabulary.

blocks.title: Saturday morning · the Hindu ceremony
blocks.setting: Saturday 22 August, 10:45 a.m., Richmond Hill Hindu Temple. The mandap set up with four pillars and marigold garlands. Priya in a red lehenga, Marcus in a sherwani. Fire ceremony about to start. Chiara and Sofia near the front, Doug further back trying to work out when to stand.

lines.t: The pandit — the priest, in Hindi — just chanted the opening mantra. Walking around the sacred fire four times is the central ritual; both bride and groom circle it. Priya told me each round represents a different vow. Keep looking.
lines.n: Il pandit — il sacerdote, in hindi — ha appena intonato il mantra d'apertura. Fare quattro giri intorno al fuoco sacro è il rito centrale; sia la sposa che lo sposo lo girano. Priya mi ha detto che ogni giro rappresenta un voto diverso. Continua a guardare.
lines.note: Walking around the sacred fire four times is the central ritual: participial clause as subject. Both bride and groom circle it: both X and Y. Each round represents: each + sing. verb.

lines.t: I didn't realise there would be so much Sanskrit. Priya is responding — she must have been practising. Marcus looks like he's holding his breath. — He is. He mentioned yesterday he was going to try not to miss a cue. — The two of them look over the moon.
lines.n: Non pensavo ci fosse così tanto sanscrito. Priya risponde — deve aver fatto pratica. Marcus sembra trattenere il respiro. — Lo sta trattenendo. Ieri aveva accennato che avrebbe cercato di non perdere nessuna battuta. — I due sembrano al settimo cielo.
lines.note: Must have been practising: past deduction (unit 18). Try not to miss: try + not + to + inf. Over the moon: idiom = extremely happy.

lines.t: Could you tell me when I'm supposed to stand up? Both of my knees are complaining and I don't want to miss the right moment. — Watch Priya's dad. When he stands, we stand. — Got it.
lines.n: Potresti dirmi quando devo alzarmi? Mi dolgono entrambe le ginocchia e non voglio perdere il momento giusto. — Guarda il padre di Priya. Quando si alza lui, ci alziamo noi. — Capito.
lines.note: I'm supposed to stand up: supposed to (unit 22). Both of my knees are complaining: both of + plural noun + plural verb. Idiomatic: knees complaining = knees hurting.

lines.t: The two families are now joined. The pandit tied the end of Priya's lehenga to the end of Marcus's sherwani — that knot stays tied for the four circles. In English we say they're tying the knot. In this ceremony they literally are. — Oh, so that's the origin.
lines.n: Le due famiglie sono ora unite. Il pandit ha legato il bordo del lehenga di Priya a quello del sherwani di Marcus — quel nodo rimane legato durante i quattro giri. In inglese diciamo che si legano il nodo. In questa cerimonia lo fanno letteralmente. — Oh, ecco l'origine.
lines.note: The pandit tied the end of X to the end of Y: factive. Tie the knot: idiom = to get married. The literal ceremony makes the idiom visible.

lines.t: This is better than my own wedding, which lasted twenty minutes at Toronto City Hall in 1979. We did make the vows and we did eat cake, but there was no sacred fire and no silk tying us together. Which is a shame.
lines.n: È meglio del mio matrimonio, durato venti minuti al Municipio di Toronto nel 1979. Abbiamo pronunciato i voti e mangiato la torta, ma non c'era né fuoco sacro né seta che ci legava insieme. Peccato.
lines.note: We did make the vows and we did eat cake: emphatic do. There was no sacred fire and no silk tying us together: both negatives, non-defining participle (tying).

notes.phrase: walking around the sacred fire is the central ritual · tying us together · trying not to miss · must have been practising
notes.note: Participial clauses as subjects, modifiers; try + not + to-inf; must + have been + -ing.

notes.phrase: both bride and groom · both my knees · both of my knees are complaining · neither of my knees · each round represents · the two of them look over the moon · tie the knot
notes.note: Both patterns and the running wedding idiom tying the knot being literalised by the ceremony.

blocks.title: Saturday night · the reception
blocks.setting: Saturday 22 August, 9:40 p.m., Toronto Botanical Garden event space, Lawrence and Leslie. Reception for 180 people. Doug has eaten three plates of dal, Marcus's uncle Peter is MC-ing. Chiara is up for her toast; she has 45 seconds of English in her head and a nervous smile. Microphone passed to her.

lines.t: Hi everyone. I'm Chiara, I bake pasticciotti with Priya at Doug's. I was going to write a long speech, but then I remembered meeting Priya for the first time, and remembered what she told me: 'Keep it short, keep it warm'. So here goes.
lines.n: Ciao a tutti. Sono Chiara, faccio pasticciotti con Priya da Doug. Avevo intenzione di scrivere un lungo discorso, ma mi sono ricordata di aver incontrato Priya la prima volta, e ricordato cosa mi aveva detto: 'Sta' breve, sta' calda'. Allora via.
lines.note: Was going to write: past intention. Remembered meeting: remember + -ing = memory of a past event. Remembered what she told me: remembered + wh-clause.

lines.t: Priya hired me when I didn't yet know the difference between a croissant and a cornetto. She said: 'Don't try to be anything other than yourself. Both the customer and the dough need honesty.' Which is the best advice I've ever received, from anyone, in any job.
lines.n: Priya mi ha assunta quando ancora non sapevo la differenza fra un croissant e un cornetto. Mi disse: 'Non cercare di essere nient'altro che te stessa. Sia il cliente sia l'impasto hanno bisogno di sincerità.' Che è il miglior consiglio che io abbia mai ricevuto, in qualunque lavoro.
lines.note: Don't try to be: try + to + inf (= attempt). Both the customer and the dough need: both X and Y + plural verb. The best advice I've ever received: present perfect + ever.

lines.t: Marcus, Priya chose you from — not many, but — let's say a few possibilities. All of them nice, none of them you. You, she chose because you made her laugh at a wedding, which was your first date — your friend's wedding, where you were a plus-one. Making someone laugh at a wedding is a strong move; marrying them two years later is a stronger one.
lines.n: Marcus, Priya ti ha scelto fra — non tante, ma — diciamo alcune possibilità. Tutte simpatiche, nessuna te. Te, ti ha scelto perché l'hai fatta ridere a un matrimonio, che era il vostro primo appuntamento — il matrimonio di un vostro amico, dove tu eri un plus-one. Far ridere qualcuno a un matrimonio è una mossa forte; sposarla due anni dopa è una più forte.
lines.note: All of them nice, none of them you: all / none of + object pronoun. Making someone laugh / marrying them: gerund as subject.

lines.t: Priya, you work ten hours and still have the energy to bring me a coffee at 4 p.m. because you noticed I was dragging. You remembered that I like it with two sugars, and you remembered me, which is the main thing. I love you. — To Priya and Marcus. Over the moon, and over Lake Ontario, cheers.
lines.n: Priya, lavori dieci ore e hai ancora l'energia di portarmi un caffè alle 16 perché hai notato che ero stanca. Ti sei ricordata che mi piace con due zollette, e ti sei ricordata di me, che è l'essenziale. Ti voglio bene. — A Priya e Marcus. Al settimo cielo, e al lago Ontario, cin cin.
lines.note: You remembered that I like it with two sugars: remember + that + clause. You remembered me: remember + object (= think of). Over the moon: idiom reprised. The toast lands at 54 seconds; Priya cries.

notes.phrase: remembered meeting Priya (memory of a past event) · remembered what she told me (recalled a fact) · remembered that I like it (recalled a fact) · remembered me (thought of a person) · don't try to be (= attempt) · try not to miss (= attempt not to)
notes.note: The three major patterns of remember and try: remember + -ing (memory) vs remember + to-inf (reminder); try + to-inf (attempt) vs try + -ing (experiment with).

notes.phrase: both X and Y · all of them · none of them · neither of · the two of them · each of · every one of
notes.note: Quantifiers with two or more. All, none, each, every take singular (or plural depending). Both, neither, either are for exactly two.

questions.q: «I remembered meeting Priya for the first time» means:
options: I had a memory of the meeting (remember + -ing = memory).
I remembered that I needed to meet her (remember + to + inf = reminder).
I tried to remember her name.
questions.why: Remember + -ing: memory of a past event. Remember + to + inf: reminder for a future action.

questions.q: «Tie the knot» means to get married.
questions.why: A fixed idiom from the ribbon ceremonies of many cultures. The literal tying at Priya's wedding gives the metaphor its etymology.

questions.q: I enjoy ___ (bake). I decided ___ (leave). I remember ___ (meet) her for the first time. Please remember ___ (call) Dora tonight.
questions.n: Enjoy + -ing. Decide + to + inf. Remember + -ing (memory). Remember + to + inf (reminder).

sections.title: Weddings, speeches, idioms, make vs do
sections.intro: Four themes: weddings and ceremonies (Canadian + Hindu overlap), speeches and humour, idioms, and the daily split between make and do.

items.n: matrimonio

ex.t: Priya and Marcus's wedding was a two-day event.
ex.n: Il matrimonio di Priya e Marcus è stato un evento di due giorni.

items.note: Wedding day. Also marriage (the institution). Nuptials: formal.

items.n: sposa · sposo

ex.t: The bride wore a red lehenga; the groom wore a sherwani.
ex.n: La sposa indossava un lehenga rosso; lo sposo un sherwani.

items.note: Bride and groom = gli sposi.

items.n: conferma di presenza (dal fr. répondez s'il vous plaît)

ex.t: Please RSVP by August 1.
ex.n: Si prega di confermare la presenza entro il 1° agosto.

items.note: French-origin acronym. On the invitation and on the response card.

items.n: lista di nozze; ufficio dello stato civile

ex.t: Their registry is at Williams Sonoma and Indigo.
ex.n: La loro lista di nozze è da Williams Sonoma e Indigo.

items.note: In Canada: a gift registry. A civil registry is the UK term for Italian comune.

items.n: ricevimento

ex.t: The reception was at the Toronto Botanical Garden.
ex.n: Il ricevimento era al Toronto Botanical Garden.

items.note: The after-ceremony party. Also receive (verb) = ricevere.

items.n: cerimonia

ex.t: The Hindu ceremony lasted ninety minutes.
ex.n: La cerimonia induista è durata novanta minuti.

items.note: Civil ceremony, religious ceremony. The pandit (Hindu priest) presides.

items.n: voto nuziale

ex.t: They exchanged vows in Sanskrit and English.
ex.n: Si sono scambiati i voti in sanscrito e inglese.

items.note: Take / exchange / renew vows. Also «for better or for worse» etc.

items.n: bar a pagamento · bar gratis

ex.t: A cash bar costs you per drink; an open bar is free.
ex.n: Un cash bar ti costa a drink; un open bar è gratis.

items.note: At Canadian weddings both exist; the hosts choose.

items.n: discorso · brindisi

ex.t: The best man gave a toast; the father of the bride gave a speech.
ex.n: Il testimone ha fatto un brindisi; il padre della sposa un discorso.

items.note: A toast is short with a glass raised; a speech is longer, from a podium.

items.n: testimone (sposo) · testimone (sposa)

ex.t: Marcus's best man is his brother Jim; Priya's maid of honour is her sister Nalini.
ex.n: Il testimone di Marcus è suo fratello Jim; la testimone di Priya è la sorella Nalini.

items.note: The two main attendants. North American wedding tradition. Bridesmaids and groomsmen: the rest.

items.n: cena a cui ciascuno porta un piatto

ex.t: A potluck wedding reception: everyone brings a dish.
ex.n: Un ricevimento potluck: ciascuno porta un piatto.

items.note: Common at smaller weddings. The host sets the structure (mains / sides / desserts), the guests fill it.

items.n: al settimo cielo (idiom)

ex.t: The couple looks over the moon.
ex.n: La coppia sembra al settimo cielo.

items.note: Very happy. British, now universal.

items.n: paura prima del matrimonio (idiom)

ex.t: Marcus had cold feet in the morning but got over it.
ex.n: Marcus aveva paura la mattina ma gli è passata.

items.note: Get cold feet: become nervous about a decision.

items.n: rompere il ghiaccio (idiom)

ex.t: The mehndi is good for breaking the ice.
ex.n: Il mehndi è utile per rompere il ghiaccio.

items.note: Idiom from unit 18 Italian equivalent. Break + the + ice.

items.n: sposarsi (idiom)

ex.t: After five years, Priya and Marcus tied the knot.
ex.n: Dopo cinque anni, Priya e Marcus si sono sposati.

items.note: Formal / semi-formal. Also get hitched (informal).

items.n: accompagnatore / accompagnatrice (al matrimonio)

ex.t: Marcus came as my plus-one to a friend's wedding — that's how we met.
ex.n: Marcus è venuto come mio plus-one al matrimonio di un amico — è così che ci siamo conosciuti.

items.note: The companion a single guest brings. Written on invitations.

items.n: nervoso · ansioso · entusiasta

ex.t: Doug was nervous; Priya was thrilled; Marcus was both.
ex.n: Doug era nervoso; Priya era entusiasta; Marcus era entrambi.

items.note: Thrilled: strongly positive. Also excited (good) vs anxious (bad).

items.n: mehndi (henné da sposa)

ex.t: Mehndi is both an art and a ceremony.
ex.n: Il mehndi è sia arte sia cerimonia.

items.note: Hindi word, now universal in Canada. Applied the day before the wedding.

items.n: pandit (sacerdote induista)

ex.t: The pandit chanted the opening mantra.
ex.n: Il pandit ha intonato il mantra d'apertura.

items.note: Hindu priest. Different from guru (teacher). Pandit means scholar.

items.n: mandap (altare induista)

ex.t: The mandap had four pillars decorated with marigolds.
ex.n: Il mandap aveva quattro pilastri decorati con calendule.

items.note: The ceremonial canopy under which the wedding happens.

items.n: umorismo

ex.t: Humour is welcome in a Canadian wedding toast.
ex.n: L'umorismo è gradito in un brindisi canadese.

items.note: Canadian spelling (unit 18). Humor is American.

items.n: un gioco da ragazzi (lit. una fetta di torta)

ex.t: The exam was a piece of cake.
ex.n: L'esame è stato un gioco da ragazzi.

items.note: Something very easy. Food idiom.

items.t: take with a grain of salt
items.n: prendere con le pinze

ex.t: Rumours about Nicola should be taken with a grain of salt.
ex.n: Le voci su Nicola si prendono con le pinze.

items.note: Food idiom. Italian: con le pinze (unit 23 IT).

items.n: in bocca al lupo (teatro / performance)

ex.t: Break a leg at your audition tomorrow!
ex.n: In bocca al lupo per il provino domani!

items.note: Body idiom. Theatre superstition — don't say good luck.

items.n: prendere in giro

ex.t: I'm just pulling your leg, don't worry.
ex.n: Ti sto prendendo in giro, non preoccuparti.

items.note: Body idiom. Joking affectionately.

items.n: spifferare un segreto

ex.t: Marcus spilled the beans about the honeymoon destination.
ex.n: Marcus ha spifferato la meta della luna di miele.

items.note: Food idiom. Also: let the cat out of the bag.

items.n: lusingare per ottenere qualcosa

ex.t: He's buttering her up for a promotion.
ex.n: La sta blandendo per una promozione.

items.note: Food idiom. Also: schmoozing.

items.n: fare brutta figura (lit. aver uova in faccia)

ex.t: I had egg on my face when I mispronounced his name three times.
ex.n: Ho fatto una brutta figura quando ho sbagliato il suo nome tre volte.

items.note: Food idiom. Public embarrassment.

items.t: it's not my cup of tea
items.n: non fa per me (lit. non è la mia tazza di tè)

ex.t: Techno music is not my cup of tea.
ex.n: La musica techno non fa per me.

items.note: Food idiom. Something you don't like.

items.n: una spalla su cui piangere

ex.t: Priya has been a shoulder to cry on more than once.
ex.n: Priya è stata una spalla su cui piangere più di una volta.

items.note: Body idiom. A supportive friend.

items.t: hit the nail on the head
items.n: cogliere nel segno (lit. colpire il chiodo sulla testa)

ex.t: You hit the nail on the head with that observation.
ex.n: Hai colto nel segno con quell'osservazione.

items.note: Idiom of accuracy.

items.t: make a decision / make a choice
items.n: prendere una decisione / fare una scelta

ex.t: I made a decision last night.
ex.n: Ho preso una decisione ieri sera.

items.note: Make for creation, for a decision, for a plan, for a mess, for a mistake.

items.n: commettere un errore

ex.t: I made a mistake with the invitations.
ex.n: Ho commesso un errore con gli inviti.

items.note: Make a mistake, not do a mistake.

items.t: make a plan / make an appointment
items.n: fare un piano / fissare un appuntamento

ex.t: I made an appointment with the pandit.
ex.n: Ho fissato un appuntamento con il pandit.

items.note: Make a plan, make a deal, make an offer, make a bet.

items.n: fare il letto

ex.t: I made the bed before leaving.
ex.n: Ho fatto il letto prima di uscire.

items.note: Make the bed (the thing you create daily). Also: make breakfast / coffee / dinner / a meal.

items.n: guadagnare / fare la differenza

ex.t: The pasticciotti make us money and make a difference.
ex.n: I pasticciotti ci fanno guadagnare e fanno la differenza.

items.note: Make = produce an outcome.

items.t: do the dishes / do the laundry
items.n: lavare i piatti / fare il bucato

ex.t: I do the dishes, you do the laundry.
ex.n: Io lavo i piatti, tu fai il bucato.

items.note: Do for routine chores. Do the dishes, do the laundry, do the shopping, do the ironing.

items.t: do your homework / do a job
items.n: fare i compiti / fare un lavoro

ex.t: Did you do your homework?
ex.n: Hai fatto i compiti?

items.note: Do = carry out a task. Do a good job, do a bad job.

items.n: fare affari / fare ricerca

ex.t: They do business with suppliers in India.
ex.n: Fanno affari con fornitori in India.

items.note: Do = engage in. Also do yoga, do exercise, do sports.

items.n: fare del tuo meglio

ex.t: Do your best — that's all we ask.
ex.n: Fai del tuo meglio — è tutto quello che chiediamo.

items.note: Do + possessive + best. Also do a favour, do good.

items.t: make vs do rule of thumb
items.n: regola generale make vs do

ex.t: Make: creation, production. Do: tasks, chores, work.
ex.n: Make: creare, produrre. Do: compiti, faccende, lavoro.

items.note: A rule of thumb. Exceptions exist (do the dishes vs make the bed), but 70% of the time this works.

sections.title: Gerund vs infinitive, both/neither/either, participles
sections.intro: Three pieces: the full gerund-vs-infinitive system; both / neither / either / all / none / each / every; participle phrases.

blocks.title: Gerund vs infinitive
blocks.rule: English verbs take different complements. (1) Verb + -ing (gerund): enjoy, finish, avoid, suggest, recommend, mind, miss, consider, imagine, deny, admit, keep (= continue), practise, dislike, risk, resist. I enjoy baking. Priya suggested leaving early. (2) Verb + to + infinitive: decide, want, need, hope, offer, refuse, promise, agree, choose, plan, pretend, afford, manage, learn, intend, deserve. I decided to leave. We hope to see you. (3) Verb + object + to + infinitive: ask, tell, want, invite, allow, encourage, remind, warn, teach, order, force, enable. She asked me to call. They invited us to come. (4) Both allowed, same meaning: begin, start, continue, like, love, hate, prefer. I like swimming / I like to swim. (5) Both allowed, different meaning: remember, forget, stop, try, regret, go on, mean. I remember meeting her (memory) vs I remembered to meet her (reminder). I stopped smoking (quit) vs I stopped to smoke (paused in order to smoke). I tried to open it (attempt) vs I tried opening it (experiment). I regret saying that (regret the past act) vs I regret to say (I'm sorry to inform you — formal register). (6) After prepositions: always -ing. I'm good at baking. Thank you for coming. (7) After adjectives: usually to-inf. It's easy to learn. Pleased to meet you.

blocks.title: Both, neither, either, all, none, each, every
blocks.rule: Quantifiers for groups. Both: two + plural verb. Both of my knees are complaining. Both Priya and Marcus are at the wedding. Both of them. Both can also be an adjective (both knees). Neither: two + singular verb. Neither of them has been to a Hindu wedding. Neither Priya nor Marcus eats meat. Either: two, usually in questions or alternatives. Either of them could win. You can take either path. All: three or more + plural (or singular for mass nouns). All of them are nice. All of the sugar is here. All my friends. None: three or more + singular (strict) or plural (common speech). None of them is / are available. None has been found. Each: one at a time + singular. Each of us has a task. Each child receives a gift. Every: three or more considered as one + singular. Every guest brought a gift. Every one of them was punctual. The two-vs-three rule: both / neither / either for exactly two; all / none / each / every for three or more. Both X and Y vs either X or Y vs neither X nor Y: coordinated conjunction patterns.

blocks.title: Participle phrases
blocks.rule: Participle phrases are reduced clauses that use the -ing (present participle) or -ed/-en (past participle) form to modify a noun or a whole clause. Two main uses. (1) Opening a sentence, giving a cause or a time: Walking into the hall, I saw my cousin. (= When I was walking…) Having thought about it, we decided to invite everyone. (= Because we had thought…) Shocked by the news, she sat down. (= After she had been shocked…) The subject of the participle and the subject of the main clause must be the same (unlike in Italian gerundio, where this is more flexible). (2) Modifying a noun: The woman wearing the red lehenga is Priya. (= who is wearing). The letter written by Doug is attached. (= that was written). This is the English equivalent of the Italian relative clause with a defining participle. Present participle (-ing) for an active action; past participle (-ed/-en) for a passive action. The participle phrase is more compact and literary than a full subordinate clause: Walking in, I saw her instead of When I walked in, I saw her.

blocks.title: Italian gerundio and participio
blocks.text: The English -ing participle phrase corresponds to Italian [[gerundio presente]] (walking in = entrando) or [[gerundio passato]] (having walked = essendo entrato). The English -ed/-en participle phrase corresponds to Italian [[participio passato]] used as an adjective (shocked = scioccato / sciccata). Italian is more flexible with the subject of the gerundio; English strictly requires same-subject in a participle phrase.

sections.title: Canadian weddings, multicultural ceremonies, speeches
sections.intro: Four pages: the Canadian wedding format, multicultural weddings in Toronto, the toast and the roast, and the potluck and gift-giving culture.

blocks.text: The Canadian wedding — in its generic Anglo-Canadian form — has a fairly reliable structure. The [[ceremony]] (religious or civil, 20 to 60 minutes), the [[cocktail hour]] (standing drinks, canapés, photos), the [[reception]] (seated dinner for 100-200 guests), the [[speeches]] (father of the bride, best man, maid of honour, usually in that order, 3-10 minutes each), the [[first dance]], the [[cake cutting]], the [[open dance floor]]. Variants: a [[Jack and Jill]] stag-and-doe party before the wedding (fundraising for the couple, popular in Ontario); a [[rehearsal dinner]] the night before; a [[morning-after brunch]]. Gifts: [[registry]] at a store (Williams Sonoma, Crate & Barrel, Hudson's Bay, Indigo); or [[cash]] (increasingly common, often as a QR code at the reception or an [[honeymoon registry]]). Not expected: silverware, china — unless the couple registers for them. Dress code: [[black tie]] (tux), [[cocktail attire]] (suit or dress), [[semi-formal]] (nice dress or khakis); the invitation says. The whole wedding typically runs $25,000 to $75,000 CAD in Toronto in 2026; small weddings go lower, destination weddings can run over 100k. In the five years since the pandemic, [[micro-weddings]] (under 30 guests) have become common.

Toronto, as the most ethnically diverse city in Canada, hosts weddings of all cultural shapes. [[Hindu]] weddings (around 400,000 Hindus in the GTA): the [[mehndi]] night (henna, music, women-centred), the [[sangeet]] (music and dance, mixed), the [[baraat]] (groom's procession on horseback or on foot), the [[mandap]] ceremony (fire, pandit, Sanskrit mantras), the [[reception]]. [[Sikh]] weddings: the [[Anand Karaj]] ceremony at a gurdwara, long and musical. [[Muslim]] weddings: the [[Nikah]] ceremony, often simple and short, followed by a [[Walima]] reception. [[Chinese]] weddings: the [[tea ceremony]], often alongside a Western ceremony and reception. [[Jewish]] weddings: the [[chuppah]] canopy, the [[ketubah]] signing, the breaking of the glass. [[Italian-Canadian]] weddings: Catholic ceremony plus five-hour sit-down reception with 200+ guests, confetti, bomboniere, the usual Italian elements adapted to Canadian space. Many [[interfaith]] weddings run two ceremonies (one each) on consecutive days, or combine elements. Priya and Marcus's wedding is an increasingly standard version: Hindu ceremony in the morning (Priya's family), Canadian reception at night (Marcus's family, friends from everywhere, and both halves of Doug's bakery).

blocks.title: The speech, the toast, the roast
blocks.text: The Canadian wedding speech is a short genre. [[Toast]] (1-3 min, with a glass raised): a sentence or two, a warm wish, a cheers. [[Speech]] (5-10 min, no glass): a longer reflection, a story, humour, affection. [[Roast]] (5-10 min, if the best man dares): light-hearted mockery of the groom, in-jokes with the couple, affectionate but risky; good roasts land, bad roasts die. The structure of a good toast: (1) [[hello and who you are]]; (2) [[how you know the person]]; (3) [[one specific memory]], short and concrete; (4) [[a wish]], short and real; (5) [[the raised glass]]. Avoid: inside jokes nobody will understand, exes, awkward sexual references, long tangents, reading the speech from the phone (print it). Length: a one-minute toast is often better remembered than a ten-minute speech. Chiara's toast is a textbook one-minute version.
Potluck, cash gifts, Jack and Jill

Three Canadian wedding-adjacent genres. [[Potluck wedding]]: a smaller, informal format where the guests bring the food. The hosts set the structure (mains / sides / desserts, assigned by invitation group), and the result is a 20-dish buffet. Common in rural Ontario, farming communities, Mennonite and Mormon weddings, and increasingly young couples looking to save money. [[Cash gift]]: increasingly standard, usually by [[e-transfer]] to the couple or in a card at the reception. Ontario average: 150-200 CAD per guest. The old «cover the cost of your plate» rule is loose: a cash gift of 100 CAD per guest is now considered polite. [[Jack and Jill]] (also [[stag-and-doe]]): a fundraising party held before the wedding, usually at a hall, with a cover charge, raffles, games, and a bar. Popular in southern Ontario and the Niagara region; less common elsewhere. The money raised offsets the wedding cost. Not a bridal shower (which is women-only), not a bachelor/ette party (which is also smaller and single-gender).
